paper.title: Mathematics Written in Sand
paper.venue: Proc. Joint Statistical Meeting of the American Statistical Association, Statistical Computing Section, 1983 (the file is the version of 22 Nov. 1983, retypeset 9 January 2001)
paper.text_read: https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~wkahan/MathSand.pdf (fetched 2026-11-19; the x - SIN(x) example and its table taken from the text, around page 29)

program.how: written for ounce-core from the statement in the paper: every p-digit decimal x in [0.001, 1) is enumerated, sin(x) is computed in double (Taylor series, no libm) and rounded to p significant decimals, F(x) = x - SIN(x) is formed exactly in integers and checked for monotonicity between consecutive p-digit decimals; no third-party code
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf --cpu=tier3`; the same source also builds natively (-DHOST) for a bit-for-bit comparison

claims_checked: p = 6: among all 2,700,000 six-digit decimals x in [0.001, 1) the only place where F(x) = x - SIN(x) decreases is x = 0.100167 -> 0.100168 (F = 0.0001674 then 0.0001670, as in the paper's table)
p = 5: the only decrease is at x = 0.010000 -> 0.010001 (F = 0.0000002 then 0)
p = 4: no decrease anywhere in [0.001, 1) (the paper: 'nowhere')
no value of sin(x) in the scan lies within 1e-8 (in units of the last place) of a rounding tie, so the decimal rounding of the double-precision sine is not in doubt

expected_values_source.what: the statement and table in the paper
expected_values_source.tolerance: exact comparison of decimal digits and of the set of exceptions. The paper does not state the domain of x; [0.001, 1) was chosen before the first run (below 0.001 SIN(x) = x for every p tested, and F is 0 there; above 1 the slope of F is too large for an exception), so 'sole exception' is checked on that domain only.

observations: the 'sole exception' claims hold exactly on the chosen domain: 1 exception for p = 6, 1 for p = 5, 0 for p = 4
negative_control: built with -DNEG_TRUNC (SIN(x) truncated instead of correctly rounded), neither published exception is found, the p = 6 and p = 5 checks fail and the program exits 1
not_checked: other precisions p, other decimal rounding rules, and x outside [0.001, 1)
the paper's other examples (VisiCalc table, the hp-15C matrix inverse, the discussion of correctly rounded arithmetic) and its argument about standards
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison here is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: ounce-core, running integer and double code, finds exactly the monotonicity failures Kahan reports for correctly rounded 6-digit and 5-digit sine and none for 4 digits, on the stated domain. It does not show the paper's wider argument.
